newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 2.

text.p: Posts & Telecommunications Ministry and Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp have reached agreement to break up telecommunication giant by establishing share-holding company. Under the plan, NTT would be divided by the end of March 1999 into one long-distance telephone company, covering both the international and domestic markets, and two local companies -- one covering eastern, the other western Japan. The three companies are expected to be maintained by the share-holding company.

The Posts and Telecommunications Ministry has decided to abolish rule requiring cellphone users to have radio station licences. The ministry will allow operators to register several hundred thousand users through a single licence from the year starting April 1997. The move will help speed up expansion of cellular phone market.

A Nihon Keizai Shimbun survey of sales rankings of Asian companies for fiscal 1995/96, except those in Japan and China, shows 43 Korean companies and 27 companies from the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) among top 100.
Taiwan and Indian saw eleven companies each in the top 100. By industry, high-tech, electricity and electronics and telecommunications businesses all gained in the rankings.
Samsung Electronics Co 64050.KS E ranked top in both sales and net profit. However, fast-growing semiconductor companies are expected to see slower growth in the year to March 1997.
IASS, a leading airport passenger handling service, plans to set up an air cargo service between Japan and the Philippines as early as next January, a joint venture with a state-run Philippines firm.
The company, capitalised at $4 million, will be owned 49 percent by IASS and 51 percent by the Philippines company. It aims for sales of three to four billion yen in the first year.

Hitachi Ltd plans to start developing an Internet-based home banking system in cooperation with the Bank of America. The new system, to be introduced by the Bank of America from August 1997, will allow personal computer users to check how much they can charge on their credit cards and enable them to change their maximum spending limit. The two companies also hope to sell the system to banks worldwide.
